messages:
alex: Heads-up — Acme reported a p99 latency spike on their /generate endpoint starting ~08:12 UTC, hits up ~3x. They say median ok but tail shooting to 8s and some 502s.

maria: seeing it in the dashboards too, p95 -> 1.2s, p99 -> 7.8s on eu-west-1. Error rate for that tenant up ~4%.

devon: quick check: KV cache hit-rate for that model dropped from 92% -> 28% at 08:11. Could be cache eviction after the config push.

jamie: deploy-bot: rollforward config v3.14 applied to runtime clusters at 08:10. Changes: default_batch_size=64, aggressive_kv_ttl=30m.

oncall-bot: Incident created: INC-3419876543. Paging oncall rotation.

alex: suspecting larger batches + cold cache causing serialization queues on CPU while waiting for GPU hot paths -> tail. Can we force smaller batches for this tenant?

maria: yes — we can set per-tenant overrides. Suggest temporary mitigation: set max_batch_size=8 and disable aggressive_kv_ttl for Acme. That should reduce queueing and make KV warmups slower but avoid spikes.

devon: +1. Also suggest routing Acme to the smaller model-variant (redwood-1-small) as fallback to reduce per-token latency while we stabilize. We have capacity in eu-west-1-dedicated pool.

alex: can we do both quickly? steps?

jamie: steps I can run now:
1) Apply tenant override:
```
POST /admin/tenants/acme/overrides
{ "max_batch_size": 8, "kv_ttl_override": "default" }
```
2) Add routing rule: route tenant acme -> redwood-1-small fallback for 1h.
3) Create rate-limit pad for acme tokens: 20rps if tail persists.

maria: I'll monitor metrics and confirm KV hit-rate and queue lengths after changes.

support-bot: Note: I've informed Acme support contact (cs@acme) that we're applying temporary throttles and fallback. Mentioned ETA ~15m.

devon: Also setting a circuit-breaker policy on the endpoint to 90th-percentile latency 2.5s -> start shedding to fallback model to avoid cascade. Command:
```
PATCH /admin/routes/generate
{ "circuit_breakers": [{ "percentile": 90, "threshold_ms": 2500, "fallback_action": "route_to: redwood-1-small" }] }
```

alex: executed tenant override and routing. Confirming flags: max_batch_size=8 set, fallback rule active.

maria: metrics: after 90s, p99 down from 7.8s -> 1.9s, error rate down to baseline. KV hit-rate slowly climbing (now 55%). No new 502s.

jamie: great. recommended next steps before we revert:
- keep overrides for 2 hours while we trace root cause of aggressive_kv_ttl regression.
- revert default_batch_size change in next config patch if it was the culprit.
- run replay of sampled requests to repro latency locally (devon to coordinate).

devon: I'll grab traces and run replay. early hypothesis: combined effect of larger batch + aggressive TTL causing cache churn and long tail queuing on CPU. will confirm.

alex: logging action items:
- devon: repro + root cause PR (24h).
- jamie: keep tenant override & routing for 2h, then review.
- maria: keep monitoring p95/p99 + create alert to auto-trigger circuit-breaker if p99 > 3s for 5m.
- support: update customer with post-mortem once we have root cause.

oncall-bot: Incident INC-3419876543 status -> mitigated.

jamie: minor note: if we need faster mitigation next time, we can script a "surge playbook" that atomically applies: per-tenant max_batch_size, queue-priority bump, fallback routing. I can draft it after this.

alex: thanks everyone. we'll keep this thread for the postmortem notes. :thumbsup:
